newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower on bearish exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower on bearish exports.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mostly lower on fresh bearish input from the export sector, traders said.
"Wheat is faltering on a lack of export demand," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

USDA early Monday said the amount of U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended January 23 totaled 8.488 million bushels. That tally was well below expectations for 16 million to 18 million bushels.
Also news Egypt bought wheat from Australia rather than the U.S. was mentioned.
"Egypt was all Australian and it's pretty quiet," a trader said.
The Egyptian state's Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills early Monday said it bought 110,000 tonnes of Australian hard wheat from the Australian Wheat Board.
Traders brushed off talk about a forecast for dry weather in the U.S. Great Plains from now through April. "It's too early to be worried about that," a trader said.
Firm cash basis markets underpinned wheat futures.
Wheat closed 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 3/4 higher, with March down 3-1/2 at $3.71-1/2 a bushel.
Smith Barney sold two million bushels of March and E.D. and F. Man plus Cargill Investor Services sold one million bushels of March, traders said.
Scattered fund and commission house buying underpinned the market, the traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 10,500 contracts, above the 9.132 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 900 March $3.90 calls and sold 900 March $3.70 calls at six to 6-1/4 cents, traders said. FIMAT also bought 175 March $3.90 call at two cents and Continental Grain bought 100 March $3.70 calls and sold 100 March $4.00 calls at eight cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 4,000 contracts, above the 2,504 traded Friday.
